requirements.requirement: usb-storage module must not be loaded / loadable on node1 immediately (now)
requirements.summary: Blacklist config written to /etc/modprobe.d/blacklist-usb-storage.conf with both 'blacklist usb-storage' and 'install usb-storage /bin/false' directives. Confirmed module was not loaded, modprobe --showconfig reflects the directive, and a manual modprobe usb_storage attempt was directly observed to fail with 'could not insert usb_storage: Invalid argument'.

requirements.requirement: usb-storage module must not load automatically after a reboot (persistent across restart)
requirements.summary: Initramfs was rebuilt via dracut -f to embed the blacklist, and the node was then actually rebooted (boot_id changed from 5fb1b173... to 7fa8cf91..., confirming a genuine restart, corroborated by global:before_prepare:node1:boot-identity and global:after_executor:node1:boot-identity). Post-restart checks directly confirm the module remained unloaded, the blacklist config persisted on disk, modprobe --showconfig still shows the blacklist directive, and a manual modprobe attempt was still blocked with the same error after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide mandatory node-restart evidence protocol executed on node1: pre-restart healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, differing post-restart boot identity, recovered service/data/config state
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id and healthy pre-restart state captured (module unloaded, blacklist present), reboot issued and acknowledged before disconnect, node polled until it returned with a different boot_id, and post-restart state re-verified as healthy (module unloaded, config persisted, block still enforced). This is directly corroborated by the fixed before_prepare and after_executor boot-identity snapshots.

overall_summary: The executor correctly blacklisted usb-storage on node1 via /etc/modprobe.d, rebuilt the initramfs for boot-time persistence, and then performed and directly verified a full reboot showing the module remained unloaded and blocked both immediately and after the restart. Both material task outcomes and the independent mandatory restart-evidence protocol are satisfied with direct, coherent evidence including a genuine boot_id transition.
limitations: lsinitrd did not list the blacklist conf file directly inside the initramfs image (only dracut module inclusion was inferred), though the post-reboot functional test (module still blocked) is a stronger and directly observed confirmation of persistence.
The reboot was a single planned restart rather than a bounded disruption test with intermediate unavailability characterization beyond one timed-out poll; recovery was nonetheless directly observed.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands (writing the blacklist conf, running dracut -f, removing the module if loaded, issuing the reboot) have a clear causal role in satisfying the task or the mandatory restart protocol. No troubleshooting experiments or abandoned mutations were observed; package-health and failed-services snapshots show no regressions after the reboot. The only incidental residue is /tmp/reboot.log, an artifact of the backgrounded reboot command used to return the acknowledgement before disconnect - a minor, expected byproduct of a necessary restart action, not an unnecessary mutation.
